configuration.formula: sum(weight / (60 + component_rank) for components containing the identity)
configuration.query_transformation: none; original query passed to both components
configuration.score_meaning: retrieval diagnostic only; not confidence, probability, authority, completeness or business state
configuration.tie_breaking: RRF score descending, then canonical identity ascending; no rounding

questions.query: A category is ready for human review, but the assessment also records a shipment-global blocker. Which aggregate action state takes precedence?
Is an open parcel already late when the evaluation clock has only just reached its promised delivery time?

With all dependent evidence available, how does an open shipment's late classification and disposition change from exactly its promised time to just after that time, while still below the escalation limit?
A verified scan gap is longer than the detection threshold but shorter than the escalation threshold, and the required inactivity evidence is complete. Which disposition applies?

This parcel has been quiet longer than the first waiting limit but less than the handoff limit. I can see a scan, yet I cannot complete the supporting inactivity checks. Should I leave it on watch or send that issue for review?
Several tracking messages describe the same unsuccessful delivery visit and carry the same attempt identifier. How many physical attempts should those messages contribute?

Before preparing an attempt-based handoff for repeated failed visits, how should duplicate messages be counted, and what support is needed once the configured unique-attempt threshold is met if no address decision is being claimed?
For a long period with no recorded movement, is seeing one timestamp enough, or must I also verify the event type and identity, the elapsed interval, history completeness and conflicting records?

I want the brief to say that repeated failed visits and an address problem both justify passing the case to my supervisor. The visit records are complete, but the address-message history is incomplete. Can I claim both reasons, and how should I handle the uncertain one?
What information belongs in the written brief prepared for a person to review a delivery exception?
How can I assemble a review brief with traceable shipment facts and unresolved items while keeping customer-identifying details out of the demonstration records?
The status and delivery records contradict one another about whether the shipment is open or closed. Is this merely an absent fact affecting one category, or does it invalidate the whole assessment?
Two approved policy bundles both appear to apply at the same moment. Can I use whichever passage looks most similar to my case and finish the ready packet?
If a synthetic demonstration performs well, may its report claim production compliance or real-world accuracy?
Under FedEx's official service rules, what is the maximum permitted delivery delay before a customer becomes entitled to compensation?
